decisions: No option or DIV/ElementId: the old cast is invalid C and the mirror declaration changes the recovered type, so preserving it is not a useful policy choice.
A one-level parenthesis move was rejected because it corrupts deeper alternation; CDeclarator groups the complete accumulated declarator.
The parser already represented pointer-to-array correctly; a parser-to-C-speller round trip now fences both mirror types.
The differential's four exported type strings are pinned exactly in a Datatype-level regression, and its non-witness passthru declaration is pinned by the existing end-to-end fixture test.

The low-mode review found no algorithmic correctness issue. Its production-function-postfix wording concern was resolved by documenting that Datatype traversal currently supplies pointer and array modifiers only.

Declaration positions (locals, array locals, return types) spelled only the declarator front, so the corrected pointer-to-array front printed unbalanced `char (*v1;` and `char (* f(int i)`. TypeSpeller::type_name now returns both halves; a local prints the back after its name and [count], a return type after the parameter list, and the rendered-line dedup keys on the back.

Every pointer/array chain up to five modifiers was spelled as a declaration, abstract type, member, local and return type and checked with gcc and clang __builtin_types_compatible_p against a typedef-built reference (1,413 assertions); the console parser round-trips the same shapes to four modifiers in a unit test.
